html:
Zanzibar is an island off the coast of Tanzania, and the name the map gives from 1715 to 1815 to the East African coast ruled from Oman, stretching from southern Somalia to the Rovuma River.

The Omani Arabs took this coast from the Portuguese in the late 1600s, capturing Fort Jesus at Mombasa in 1698 after a siege of nearly three years. Rule came from Muscat across the sea.

The island's great age came next. In the early 1800s Omani planters began growing cloves on Zanzibar and Pemba, worked by enslaved Africans, and the islands became the world's main source of cloves. Sultan Said bin Sultan moved his court from Muscat to Zanzibar around 1840. Caravans led by traders such as Tippu Tip went deep into the interior for ivory and captives, and Zanzibar ran the largest slave market on the coast.

After Said died in 1856 his sons split Oman and Zanzibar into separate sultanates. Under British pressure the slave market closed in 1873, and Zanzibar became a British protectorate in 1890. It became independent in 1963. In April 1964, after a revolution overthrew the sultan, Zanzibar joined Tanganyika to form Tanzania.
sum: Zanzibar is an island off the coast of Tanzania, and the name the map gives from 1715 to 1815 to the East African coast ruled from Oman, stretching from southern Somalia to the Rovuma River.
